rows.author: F105
rows.title_full: CALL FOR THE SUPPORT OF THE HOUSE IN THE UPCOMING ILO HIGH LEVEL MISSION TO THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Overseas Filipino Workers ( O F W S )
rows.abstract: Encouraged the Body to support the International Labor Organization (ILO) High Level Fact Finding Mission on Sept. 22 to 29, 2009, to give justice to Filipino workers who are victims of trade union and human rights violations.  Added that Party-List Anakpawis had filed a resolution on the issue of deployment of military in workplaces and expressed hope that the concerned Committee would conduct an investigation thereon.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2009-09-23

rows.author: F037
rows.abstract: Discussed the crucial question of whether former President Joseph E. Estrada is constitutionally and legally eligible to run for president.  Stated that the former President is not eligible for any reelection and then cited as explanations, Art. VII, Sections 2 & 4 among others.  Cited that former Pres. Estrada was convicted of plunder and was sentenced to suffer the penalty of reclusion perpetua and the accessory penalties of civil interdiction and perpetual abolute disqualification from public office.  Stated that base from the provisions of Sec. 4, Art. VII of the Constitution which bars the President from any reelection, and the specific whereas clause of Pres. Arroyo's executive clemency, the former President is ineligible to serve again as President.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Remulla and Rodriguez.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: CALL FOR THE FILING OF ADMINISTRATIVE CHARGES AGAINST DEPUTY NATIONAL SECURITY ADVISER SINGSON FOR VIOLATING THE ANTI-VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN ACT AND MISUSE OF FUNDS
rows.title_short: Case Against Asst. National Security Adviser Chavit Singson
rows.abstract: Denounced the physical abuse and violence committed by Dep. Nat'l Security Adviser \"Chavit\" Singson against his common-law wife Rachelle Tiongson.  Said that she is bothered by Mr. Singson's shameless and unrepentant admission that he is a wife batterer and underscored that there is no place in the Cabinet or in any government office for an offender who violates RA 9262 or the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children (VAWC) Act of 2004.  Stressed that Mr. Singson also failed to abide with the mandate of RA 6713 or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.  Urged the House to revisit the Anti-VAWC Law to reeducate them on the rights of women; and for the Members to work together to stop domestic violence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2009-09-23

rows.author: E057
rows.title_short: Nhas Plan To Sell And Develop Some Lands In Q.c.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Crisologo and Rodriguez.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F024
rows.title_short: Harassment And Extortion Of N B I In Iloilo City
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cerilles. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.abstract: Referred to the statement made by the Department of Energy that there might be power shortage during the 2010 national elections, and stressed that her constituents in Marinduque are already suffering from daily brownouts such that there is no need to wait for said election to feel the debilitating effects of the power crisis.  Requested for an emergency inquiry to determine why the power situation has deteriorated rapidly, and asked all concerned to come up with short and long term solutions to address the problem.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2009-09-23

rows.author: F070
rows.title_full: EFFECTS OF TYPHOON \"ONDOY\" IN MARIKINA CITY
rows.title_short: Rehabilitation Of Marikina After Typhoon \" Ondoy \"
rows.abstract: Spoke on the recent tragedy brought about by typhoon Ondoy which affected the entire Metro Manila including the City of Marikina.  Urged the Body to fast track enactment of the measure on the Phil. Disaster Management Act which aims to seek the formulation of the disaster management program and the creation of the National Disaster and Management Commission tasked to establish the capacity of people and communities to prepare for disaster and other similar eventualities.  Underscored the need to amend the Local Government Code to enable local government units to utilize calamity funds for disaster preparedness and not only during times of disasters.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2009-10-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Casino, Golez, Apostol and Villanueva.  Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F035
rows.title_full: HOW TYPHOON \"ONDOY\" RAVAGED THE 2ND DISTRICT OF VALENZUELA CITY
rows.title_short: Devastating Effects Of Typhoon \" Ondoy \" In Valenzuela
rows.abstract: Informed his colleagues of the extraordinary and widespread devastating effects of tropical storm \"Ondoy\" on the Camanawa (Caloocan, Malabon, Navotas and Valenzuela) area which included his district in Valenzuela City and which, together with Quezon City, comprises the downstream areas of Tullahan River that runs from La Mesa Dam to Manila Bay.  Raised  several issues regarding disasters:  whether La Mesa Dam released water during the storm without prior notice; whether SOP govern the operations of the dam; and whether the MMDA and the local governments of Quezon City and Camanawa have the capability to respond to extraordinary acts of nature.  Proposed that the GSIS, SSS and Pag-IBIG extend emergency loans to the victims of typhoon Ondoy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2009-09-29
rows.remarks: Change of referral from Metro Mla. Devt. Authority to National Defense and Security on 2009-10-06.  Interpellation by Reps. Bello and Cerilles.

rows.author: E035
rows.title_full: NEED TO PASS THE DISASTER RISK REDUCTION MANAGEMENT BILL IN VIEW OF DESTRUCTION BROUGHT BY TYPHOON \"ONDOY\"
rows.abstract: Spoke on the need to pass the Disaster Risk Reduction Management (DRRM) Bill in the light of the disaster brought about by typhoon Ondoy.  Informed the Body that said Bill provides for the creation of an independent DRRM authority which seeks to institutionalize disaster preparedness in all levels of government, integrate disaster risk management to the people and reduce the loss of life and property to disasters through forward planning and hasten the rehabilitation of those adversely affected through sustained action.  Urged the Members to pass the Bill and demonstrate the same faith, courage, compassion and selflessness exhibilted by fellow Filipinos during these trying times.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2009-10-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla, Cuenco, Biazon,  and Romualdo.  Manifestation by Reps. Ocampo and Plaza.  For referral to where the DRRM bill was referred to.

rows.author: E003
rows.title_full: CALL FOR A STOP TO POLITICAL BICKERING IN VIEW OF THE ONSLAUGHT OF TYPHOON \"ONDOY\"
rows.abstract: Focused on the devastation caused by typhoon Ondoy, and noted how politicians, esp. the so-called \"presidentiables,\" have resorted to infomerciasl instead of attending to the real problems of the government and helping the typhoon victims.  Asked their colleagues in the Senate to stop the mudslinging and instead bring their cause to the proper forum.  Suggested that government officials and agencies help enforce the law; perform their duties with integrity and accountability; and work together to prevent costly flooding and landslides.  Informed the Body of a resolution he filed in this regard and of his wish to inspect the weather forecasting equipment of PAGASA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2009-10-06

rows.author: A043
rows.title_short: Additional Ninth Ray To The Philippine Flag
rows.abstract: Commended the advocacy to add a ninth ray to the Philippine flag to give equal significance to the Muslim struggle.  Stressed that 1) this distorted the historical reality in the 19th century because the Muslims never participated in the 1896 revolution despite Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo's invitation to join the same; and 2) the armed struggle of the Bangsamoro people started by the MNLF and pursued by the MILF, MNLF Reformists, and smaller radical groups was premised on the belief and conviction in an ancient Moro nation led by the Sultans of Maguindanao and Sulu and the Islamic mandate to recover and re-establish the lost Islamic State independent and separate from the Filipino nation state.  Concluded that forcing the issue that Muslims were part of the revolution while fueling the social bias against them with the idea that they had been absent in a crucial period of the revolution, would only divide the nation.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Datumanong and manifestation by Reps. Coscolluela and Escudero.

rows.author: E057
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED CONCERN OVER THE JOINT VENTURE AGREEMENT BETWEEN AYALA LAND, INC. AND THE NATIONAL HOUSING AUTHORITY
rows.title_short: Alleged Joint Venture Agreement Between Ayala Land, Inc. And The National Housing Authority ( N H A ) Involving Lands Of The Veterans Memorial Center, Kidney Center And Lung Center
rows.abstract: Expressed vehemently that she was not in favor of any development in the East and North Triangle areas because the funds to be used would be that of the Quezon City government.  Requested that the matter be referred to the Committee on Ecology and that the NHA be investigated for abuse of power.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2009-09-29
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Crisologo, Rogriguez R., and manifestation by Rep. Defensor.

rows.author: F024
rows.title_full: COMPLAINED OF THE EXTORTION AND HARASSMENT COMMITTED AGAINST HIM BY THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
rows.abstract: Related the harassment and extortion activities made on him by confidential agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)in Iloilo City with regard to an alleged shooting incident involving his brother-in-law last March 2009.  Requested for a full-blown investigation on the matter which will include a review of RA157 or the NBI Act to determine whether there is a duplication of roles of the PNP and the NBI.  Said that he does not want the Internal Afairs of the NBI to investigate these people to prevent the case from being \"whitewashed.\"  Added that he has already expressed reservation to interpellate on the NBI budget so that he could propose a P1 budget for the NBI-Region VI
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2009-09-29

rows.author: F067
rows.title_short: Laguna Lake Development Authority ( L L D A ) Bill / Laguna Floods
rows.abstract: Spoke about the devastation in lives and properties caused by tropical storm Ondoy, particularly in Sta. Cruz, Laguna.  Reiterated the call he made to make an urgent appeal for the rehabilitation of Laguna Lake and informed the Body that Speaker Nograles had certified his HB2963 as a priority measure.  Described how the present deteriorating state of Laguna Lake had contributed to the damage caused by storm Ondoy.  Said that Sen. Gordon has graciously accepted to sponsor the Senate version of the LLDA Bill and likewise called on the President to certify it as an urgent measure.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Cojuangco, Golez and Castro.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: D077
rows.title_full: CALLED ON MAYOR BERNABE TO EXPLAIN HIS QUESTIONABLE TRANSACTIONS IN PARANAQUE
rows.abstract: Asked Mayor Florencio M. Bernabe Jr. of Paranaque City, in the spirit of transparency and public service, to respond to the questions he raised re: 1)whether the amount of P30 million was disbursed before the 2007 elections as cash advances from the General Fund; 2)whether the garbage hauling and disposable contracts from 2004 to 2007 were not subjected to public bidding; and 3) whether the decorative street lights along Roxas Boulevard were overpriced at P49 million.  Urged the Office of the Ombudsman as well as the House Committees on Good Government, and Oversight to investigate the issues he had raised.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2009-11-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Plaza.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F122
rows.title_full: PAID TRIBUTE TO TEACHERS IN CELEBRATION OF \"WORLD TEACHERS' DAY\"
rows.abstract: Acknowledged the representatives of the Teachers Dignity Coalition and said that the tribute takes note of the possible impact of the global economic crisis on the avowed goal of government worldwide to achieve the Education for All (EFA) goals by 2015.  Enumerated the various issues and concerns necessary for the stability of the teaching force in the public sector that he asked the Members to take congnizance of as they work with teachers in molding educated and responsible citizens.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bello.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E046
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED HIS SENTIMENTS ON THE MANNER COMELEC COMMISSIONERS HANDLED THE ALAGAD CASE
rows.title_short: Commission On Election ( C O M E L E C )
rows.abstract: Referred to the budget hearing of the COMELEC wherein he registered his negative sentiments against the remnants of the Abalos Commission, in particular, Commissioner Rene Sarmiento, in behalf of the orphaned constituents of his Party-List Alagad.  Concluded that the COMELEC is the only constitutionally mandated body to supervise the election of the country's leaders.  Enjoined his colleagues to support Commissioner Melo to help clean the Office of its misfits.  Demanded the resignation of Commissioner Sarmiento.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2009-11-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Osabel.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F105
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR A REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT'S ECONOMIC POLICIES IN VIEW OF CRISIS POLICIES IN VIEW OF CRISIS CAUSED BY TYPHOON \"ONDOY\"
rows.abstract: Expressed his opinion on what should be the direction of the country's economic policies vis-a-vis the huge debt, budget deficit and the effect of global finanical crisis.  Opined that the bailout should focus on the people through legislated wage increase, upholding the right of workers to form a union, stopping contractualization and allocating funds to service the needs of the people, among others, instead of debt payment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2009-11-10

rows.author: D017
rows.title_short: Massive Effects Of Flooding In Pangasinan
rows.abstract: Stressed that the uncontrolled release of water in San Roque Dam in Pangasinan and the resultant river overload and dike breaching caused the recent massive flooding in his district.  Relayed in detail what happened in the province.  Stressed the need for a dam water release protocol and a congressional inquiry on the incident to include the Representatvies of the sixth, fifth, third and second districts of Pangasinan and to be co-chaird by him.
rows.remarks: Interpellated by Rep. Padilla.  Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F106
rows.abstract: EXPRESSED THE SOLIDARITY OF THE ALLIANCE OF RURAL CONCERNS (ARC) PARTY-LIST WITH THE SAVE SIERRA MADRE NETWORK (SSMN) WHOSE MEMBERS SHOWED THEIR PROTEST AGAINST THE LAIBAN DAM PROJECT TO BE CONSTRUCTED IN TANAY, RIZAL.  VOICED OUT THE REASONS OF THE COALITION FOR OPPOSING THE PROJECT, PUSHED FOR THE ADOPTION OF THE FF ALTERNATIVES:  REHABILITATE WAWA DAM AND UTILIZE THE 11 RIVERS IN THE SIERRA MADRE.  AGREED THE NEED TO PROTECT THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS IN THE SIERRA MADRE AND TO DEMAND A CONGRESSIONAL INQUIRY INTO THE PROJECT.  CALLED ON THE MWSS TO DESIST FROM PURSUING JOINT VENTURE WITH THE SAN MIGUEL BULK WATER COMPANY. EMPHASIZED THAT HUMAN RIGHTS SHOULD BE PROTECTED FOREMOST OVER THE SUPPOSED BENEFITS OF THE LAIBAN DAM.

rows.author: F105
rows.abstract: RECALLED THE INCIDENTS OF SHOOTING AND DEATH OF SEVERAL FARMERS AND PLANTATION WORKERS OF HACIENDA LUISITA ON NOV. 16, 2004, WHO WERE MEMBERS OF THE CATLU AND ULWU.  HE SAID THAT THE STRIKE WAS STAGED TO PROTEST UNFAIR LABOR PRACTICES AND TO DEMAND THE ABOLITION OF THE STOCK DISTRIBUTION OPTION (SDO) WHICH THEY CONSIDERED A FAKE AGRARIAN REFORM SCHEME. APPEALED FOR JUSTICE TO THE VICTIMS OF THE MASSACRE AND FOR THE REPEAL OF THE ASSUMPTION OF JURISDICTION ORDER AND THE STOCK DISTRIBUTION OPTION (SDO) UNDER THE CARP AS IT IS NOT AN ALTERNATIVE TO GENUINE LAND REFORM.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_short: Mga Martir Ng Hacienda Luisita Massacre
rows.abstract: FOCUSED ON THE VICTIMS OF THE EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLINGS THAT HAPPENED IN CENTRAL AZUCARERA DE TARLAC AND LAMENTED THAT THE COJUANGCO-AQUINO FAMILIES HAVE CONTINUED THEIR REIGN OVER HACIENDA LUISITA DESPITE THE PRES'L AGRARIAN REFORM COUNCIL'S DECISION FOR THE FORMER TO REVOKE THAT ANTI-FARMER SDO. DISCLOSED THAT THE OWNERS HAVE USED THE PROVISIONS OF THE CARP TO SUSTAIN THEIR POWER AND OWNERSHIP THEREOF. NOTED HOW SEN. AQUINO WASHED HIS HANDS FROM THE CHALLENGE POSED BY THE FARMERS TO HELP RESOLVE THE ISSUE. SAID THAT THE VICTIMS HAVE NOT BEEN GIVEN THE JUSTICE DUE THEM AND ENJOINED HIS COLLEAGUES TO HELP IN THE FIGHT FOR A GENUINE LAND REFORM PROGRAMS.
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Marcoleta.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: D062
rows.title_short: C C P / N P A In Sorsogon
rows.abstract: RELAYED HOW HE WAS BEING WRONGLY IMPLICATED AS A SUPPORTER OF COMMUNIST REBELS IN HIS DISTRICT.  INQUIRED INTO THE CAPABILITY OF THE MILITARY TO GUARANTEE PUBLIC SAFETY AND A PEACEFUL CAMPAIGN PERIOD FOR THE 2010 ELECTIONS; WHETHER THE INCIDENTS LINKING HIM TO THE COMMUNISTS WERE POLITICALLY MOTIVATED; AND THE STATUS OF THE PEACE TALKS BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT AND THE CPP-NDF-NPA.

rows.author: F101
rows.title_short: For Insertion Into The Records Of The House.

rows.author: F100
rows.abstract: Motion to move that his speech on the VFA he delivered on September 8, 2009 be referred to the appropriate committee.(J24, p.129)

rows.author: C127
rows.title_full: ISSUES SURROUNDING THE MINING PROJECTS IN MINDORO
rows.abstract: Relayed the opposition of different private sector groups, indigenous communities and LGUs in Mindoro Occidental to certain approved mining projects in the province.  Said that the agencies concerned and the mining companies failed to comply with the provisions of the Phil. Mining Act, the Local Government Code and the Indigenous People's Rights Act which require them to thoroughly study the direct and indirect effects of the project on nature, health, life, and climate; as well as to ensure their social acceptability and credible and realistic consultation with the stakeholder concerned.  Commended the LGUs of Mindoro Oriental for their stance and urged his colleagues to heed the appeal of the Mindorenos to investigate the DENR, the MGB (Mines and Geoscience Bureau), the EMB (Environmental Management Bureau) and the NCIP (National Commission on Indigenous Peoples).
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Valencia, Hontiveros, Casino and dela Cruz.  Manifestations by Reps.Umali (A.) and Ocampo.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_full: \"REFLECTIONS\" - Need for the Filipino people to unite in order to solve the country's problems
rows.abstract: Spoke on \"Reflections\" on the situations of our individual lives and of the country in pilgrimage to the solutions of the problems such as constant prayer and effort that would finally lead to the fulfillment of their aspirations for the country.  Stressed that Members have the same heart desiring for the country's greatness and that they have made the Republic of the Philippines as one, and ecouraged his colleagues to adopt a federal system of government.

rows.author: F109
rows.title_full: ON THE DEMISE OF FORMER SECTORAL REP. REY TEVES
rows.title_short: Tribute To Late Rep. Rey Magno Teves
rows.abstract: Talked about the greatness of a former colleague in the House, the late Rey Magno Teves, who always pushed for his advocacies especially that of the Mindanaoans.
rows.remarks: Manifestations by Reps. Hontiveros, Rodriguez and Ilagan.

rows.author: D017
rows.abstract: Discussed the operational accountability of government offices and informed the Body on the achievements and continuing success of the Pres'l Anti-Smuggling Group (PASG); urged those who have legitimate gripes against it to present their evidence instead of judging by innuendo, and called on the incumbent head thereof to keep up the good work.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2009-11-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committees on Good Government and Public Accountability and Oversight

rows.author: F101
rows.title_full: NEED TO UPLIFT TEACHERS AND THE OVERALL EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM
rows.abstract: Rose to defend and support teachers, students and the whole of the Philippine education.  Called on his colleagues and other government agencies in charge of education to work together for the upliftment of teachers in public and private schools in the overall educational system of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2010-01-19

rows.author: A024
rows.title_full: MAGUINDANAO MASSACRE AND THE IMPOSTITION OF MARTIAL LAW IN THE PROVINCE
rows.abstract: Denounced the recent massacre of civilians and journalists in his district in Ampatuan, Maguindanao, and stressed that the government must bring the perpetrators to justice even as he said that it must observe due process.  Disagreed to Pres.Proc. No. 1959 placing said province in a state of martial law and suspending the writ of habeas corpus.  Stressed that said Proc.1959 had created more problems for the people as it has unduly hampered their fundamental civil and political liberties.  Appealed to Congress to make a thorough study and appropriate decision regarding said Proclamation as he believes that the declaration of a state of emergency is more than enough to restore normalcy in Maguindanao.  Disagreed on the transferring of supervision over the ARMM from OP to the DILG as it contradicts the Constitution and that they should follow the rule of succession which is prescribed by RA No. 9054.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-01-19
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bello, Padilla, Marcoleta, Lagman and Antonino-Custodio.  Manifestation by Rep. Ocampo.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A094
rows.title_full: RELOCATION OF INFORMAL SETTLERS IN THE MANGGAHAN FLOODWAY AND OTHER WATERWAYS IN METRO MANILA
rows.abstract: Talked about the relocation of informal settlers from danger zones and said that while there is a directive from Pres. Macapagal-Arroyo not to allow informal settlers to return to their houses in danger zones, there was no place where they could relocate.  Called on the officials of different agencies esp. the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA), and the National Housing Authority (NHA), to give assistance to said informal settlers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2010-01-19
rows.remarks: Manifestations by Reps. Osabel and Maza.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F100
rows.title_full: IMPOSITION OF MARTIAL LAW IN MAGUINDANAO
rows.abstract: Said that he was surprised about the issuance of Proclamation No. 1959 and maintained that it was unconstitutional based on several grounds he mentioned.  Opined that said proclamation was never intended for the victims of the Maguindanao massacre but was being used to perpetuate President Macapagal-Arroyo in power.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-01-19

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: VICTIMS OF THE MAGUINDANAO MASSACRE FROM SOUTH COTABATO AND GENERAL SANTOS CITY
rows.abstract: Stated that she wants the names of the victims of the Maguindanao massacre to be documented in the House Record amidst the technicalities of the proclamation of martial law in Maguindanao.  Stressed that one of the reasons for Mindanao violence is the proliferation of firearms and the employment of civilian volunteers organizations (CVOs) by the so-called warlords as private armies.  Maintained that the government should implement the policies and empower the police and military in confiscating the loose firearms and that Congress should look at some policy questions in the exercise of its oversight function.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2010-01-19
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Locsin.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: CLIMATE CHANGE POLICIES TO BE NEGOTIATED IN COPENHAGEN
rows.abstract: Focused on the issue of climate change negotiations that had begun in Copenhagen.  Stressed that the steadfastness of leaders from developing countries in the negotiations may spell the difference between a pro-people and an ineffective climate policy that will burden the developing world.  Called on the negotiators to defend the position of Philippine delegation, which embodies a good and cooperative relationship between some agencies and individuals in government and civil society groups.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2010-01-19

rows.author: D069
rows.title_short: Ruling On The Protest Against Gov. Padaca
rows.abstract: Asked that immediate action be made by all institutions concerned to address the grave scandal that once again hit the COMELEC, lest the confidence of the public in its ability and integrity to hold fair and honest elections would be in peril.  Cited the case of Isabela Gov. Grace Padaca and asked for an inquiry in aid of legislation on the obvious attempt, with the help of the COMELEC, to thwart the governor.  Said that the appropriate investigating agencies should conduct their own investigations to prosecute those who will be found responsible.

rows.author: F057
rows.title_short: Construction Of Bioethanol Plant In Cagayan De Oro City
rows.abstract: Stressed that several groups have opposed the construction of a bioethanol plant in Cagayan de Oro City as it would destroy the river of said area which is the only source of potable water.  Informed the Body that the Committee on Ecology had unanimously approved a motion that the DENR, specificaaly the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB), hold in abeyance the issuance of an Environment Compliance Certificate (ECC) to the Alsons Consolidate Resources until such time that the House shall have come out with a conclusion in its investigation of said company.  Lamented that a certain EMB director name Mr. Julian J. Amador issued a memorandum that an ECC may be issued to the Alsons Consolidated Resources.  Pointed out that said memo had rendered the work of the Committee nugatory as some people in the DENR are succumbing to follow ups by particular groups who would like to secure midnight ECC approvals.  Moved that Mr. Amador be summoned.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2009-12-15
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Ecology.

rows.author: F011
rows.title_full: NEWS ARTICLES ABOUT ALLEGED WARLORDISM AND RAMPANT LAWLESSNESS IN LANAO DEL SUR
rows.title_short: Allegations As Warlords With Private Armies
rows.abstract: Defended his family from allegations that they are warlords with private armies. Called on the media and various sectors of society to be more responsible and accurate in their reporting.  Underscored that the absence of peace in Lanao del Sur is not the result of armed force, but of poor education, hunger, poverty, an unstable economy, and poor access to health services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2010-01-19

rows.author: A094
rows.title_full: INACTION OF THE DOJ ON THE CASE INVOLVING THE ASSASSINATION OF A PEASANT LEADER IN JUNE 2009
rows.title_short: The Case Involving The Assassination Of Atty. Crispin Perez Jr.
rows.abstract: Pointed out the inaction of the Secretary of the Department of Justice Agnes Devanadera on the case involving the assassination of Atty. Crispin Perez Jr., a radio broadcaster in San Jose Occidental Mindoro.  Recalled that it was the Secretary herself who said that cases involving the killing of media persons would be given priority under her stewardship.  Averred that under DOJ rules, the Department is given two months to resolve cases and that priority cases must not take more than one to two weeks to resolve. Appealed that the Body take the necessary steps to ensure that the processes of justice are observed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2010-01-19

rows.author: D089
rows.title_full: FIREWORKS INDUSTRY IN BULACAN
rows.abstract: Spoke on the issues concerning the fireworks and pyrotechnics industry in line with the forthcoming Fourth World Pyro-Olympics in January 2010. Expressed hope that the local industry would be supported to enable it to produce fireworks with state-of-the-art-quality.  Proposed that the Bureau of Customs and the PNP implement the measures preventing smuggling and the illegal importation of said products. Proposed that the government set a clear, comprehensive and responsive policy in promoting, modernizing and developing the fireworks industry; that RA No. 7183 or the National Fireworks Industry be amended to make it more relevant and responsive to development that have taken place in the domestic and international markets; and that a national pyrotechnic industry development freamework be crafted by the PNP and multisectoral agencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2010-01-19
rows.remarks: Interpellation of Rep. Gunigundo. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: D051
rows.abstract: Focused on the Maritime Industry Authority's (Marina)refusal to accept responsibility for the numerous sea tragedies in the country, and the battle being wagedd by USec. and Marina Administrator Elena Bautista against Congress. Stressed that Ms. Bautista has the power to suspend the licensing operation of ships that are not fit to travel on seas, and noted how she blames the Members for sitting on the proposed Phil. Maritime Act of 2009. Cited several tragedies that have occurred during the time of Ms. Bautista, as well as her numerous official trips abroad, and asked his colleagues to seek her removal from public office.

rows.author: F081
rows.title_short: Disqualification Case Against Rep. Dan Fernandez
rows.abstract: Recalled the disqualification case filed against him by the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal (HRET)and informed the Body of the Supreme Court ruling reinstating him as the duly elected Representative of the First District of Laguna. Expressed his gratitude to Speaker Norgrales for continuously giving aid to his district despite the fact that it had no sitting Representative especially during Ondoy and Pepeng typhoons, and for believing in him even when threatened with the filing of a case with the Committee on Ethics for failure to execute the decision of the HRET.  Thanked Rep. Chipeco, the lone Member of the House contingent to the Electoral Tribunal who voted in his favor.

rows.author: F122
rows.abstract: Clarified a reported statement of Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago in the Daily Tribune implying that he is intending to attack the Senator and defend DILG Secreatry Ronaldo Puno.  Said that he will not abuse the privileges granted to him as a legislator by attacking Sen. Santiago or anybody and expressed that these matters should be outside the concerns of the Chamber and no longer be the subjects of privilege speeches at all. Clarified that he intends to pursue with more vigor their advocacies for educational reform, including overseas workers.

rows.author: F105
rows.title_short: Nomination Process And Appointment Of The Next Supreme Court Justice
rows.abstract: Cited the Administration's obvious attempt to expedite the nomination process and appointment of the next Supreme Court Justice and alleged that Pres. Macapagal-Arroyo intends to appoint a Justice that would ensure her \"Peace of mind,\" in terms of facing legal issues, once she steps down from the presidency.  Cited two basic arguments that need to be addressed in the appointment of the next Supreme Court Justice. Questioned the alleged effort of the Administration to \"speed up\" the nomination process and appointment of the Supreme Court Justice and asked Supreme Court Justice Reynato Puno and the Members of the House to resist such desperate moves.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_short: Massacres And Forced Disappearances Of Peasants And Farmers
rows.abstract: Stated that once again the farmers and peasants are in the streets marching towards Malacanang not only to commemorate the unfortunate deaths of 13 peasants and farmers but also to reiterate their call for genuine agrarian reform and justice. Stressed that the farmers and peasants would continue to seek land for the landless and particularly seek for justice, citing the experiences of farmers from EO No. 229, which provided for the stock dividend option under the CARP, the deaths of 561 farmers from the Oplan Bantay Laya counter-insurgency program, the massacre in Hacienda Luisita and numerous incidents of massacres and forced disappearances of peasants and farmers in the countryside.

rows.author: F102
rows.abstract: Opined that among the Body's priorities was to determine the bicameral conferees on the Disaster Risk Reduction Management Bill as he reminded the Members of the devastation wrought by the recent earthquake in Haiti and typhoons \"Pepeng\" and \"Ondoy\".  Cited the need for the Body to approve the Freedom Information Bill, the Reproductive Health Bill, and the Crop Insurance Bill and to immediately act on HRs 1520 and 1521, re: escalating election-related violence and the readiness of the Comelec to hold automated elections.

rows.author: F011
rows.abstract: Spoke on how the whole peace process in Mindanao has been held hostage by politics from within the national government as the latter has failed to provide even the most basic amenities in the region.  Stressed that the government must make the peace process a national policy and pointed out that a special plan is needed for the Muslims to restore their trust in government and that any peace process in Mindanao must be measured against the standards of nutrition, education and self-government because unless the causes are adressed, any peace that is forged is just a means of preserving an unjust status quo leading to bigger tensions.

rows.title_short: Loan For The R O - R O Vessel
rows.abstract: Informed his colleagues that Sandiganbayan granted his motion for the reinvestigation and retrial of the case against the Prov'l Gov't of Oriental Mindoro for extending a loan in 1994 for the repair of a private roll-on roll-off (RO-RO)vessel to speed up the delivery of relief supplies to calamity victims.  Thanked the Body for adopting HR 209 which expressed support for said petition.

Called attention to the sufferings of the people of Mindanao and expressed hope that Congress would approved the convening of a Constitutional Convention for the purpose of changing the system of government and instituting reforms in Mindanao.  Expressed appreciation for the creation of the Caraga State University as he opined that education is the only way to ensure poverty alleviation.

rows.author: D009
rows.abstract: Called the attention of the Body to the corrupt activities and betrayal of public trust of Bohol Gov. Erico B. Aumentado and the brazen acts of partisan politics by PNP Prov'l Director, Sr. Superintendent Anthony Lao Obenza. Stressed that Gov. Aumentado and Superintendent Obenza, together with the former's lawyer, Atty. Salvador Deputado, are planning to destroy and demolish the governor's political adversaries. Appealed to the Members to urge the Comelec to immediately replace said police officer and take a serious look at the prevailing political atmosphere in Bohol as everything they see is farm from the truth.

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate commitee.
